brief_rationale: All eight responsibility-chain items are met with no serious or minor in-chain errors. The doctor conducted thorough emergency screening, correctly contextualized post-ACS/post-PCI risks, clarified timeline/status through workspace and dialogue, addressed medication safety with specific antiplatelet verification, created a detailed executable plan with medications and emergency thresholds, handled privacy barriers with minimal-necessary framing, and maintained appropriate uncertainty without overreach. Three high-order points were actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact: timeline reconstruction (HO1), privacy barrier navigation (HO2), and dynamic reprioritization (HO4). The trajectory achieved valid closure with safe, executable, and traceable handoff. Grade 5 requires two completed high-order points; three were completed.

HO3 requires an ambiguous family interpretation of a specific result to verify. The family did not provide ambiguous result statements like 'tests were normal' or conflicting values. The family's uncertainty was about timeline and medication status, not about interpreting specific test results as normal/abnormal. The case records contained procedure notes and orders, but no discordant family interpretations of troponin/ECG values were presented.
